$comment: The judgement calls — everything that cannot be extracted from code. Props, tokens, tests and adoption are generated; this file holds what a human decided. Keep it honest: it is what the inventory site and AGENTS.md publish.
summary: Transient, non-blocking confirmation of an outcome. Fired imperatively via toast(), rendered by one ToastProvider.
description: Toast announces that something finished — a save landed, an export is ready, a request failed. It queues, auto-dismisses, pauses its timers on hover/focus/window blur, and never takes focus. The imperative toast() API works from any code, React or not; the Provider at the app root renders the queue.
useFor: Confirming background or async outcomes: 'Changes saved', 'Export ready'
Failures of an action the user just took, with a retry action (variant="danger")
Offering a time-boxed undo after a destructive action — alongside a persistent undo path
dontUseFor: Errors the user must resolve or keep seeing — use Banner, which persists and stays findable
Form validation — inline, next to the field; a toast disappears before the user finds the field
Anything requiring a decision or reading time — that is Dialog; a toast with two actions is a Dialog in denial

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the toast viewport — the documented route for keyboard users to reach an action before the timeout (Radix systems default to F8)
Through each toast's action and close button, then out of the viewport
Activates the focused action or close button

provides: role="status" (polite) for info/success/warning; role="alert" (assertive) only for danger — a success must not interrupt the screen reader mid-sentence
Focus is never moved when a toast appears — appearing is not an interaction
Timers pause on viewport hover, on focus within, and on window blur, so a toast is not dismissed while unread
A close button on every toast; auto-dismiss is a convenience, never the only exit
Queueing beyond the visible limit (default 3), FIFO, instead of stacking over the page
consumerMustProvide: A persistent alternate path to any action offered in a toast — 'Undo' here must also exist in a menu or history, or a missed toast is data loss
A title that carries the meaning in text; the variant colour and icon are reinforcement, not the message
Exactly one ToastProvider, at the app root — two providers means two competing viewports
limitations: A toast is only discoverable while visible. Screen-reader users hear it once; sighted users who glanced away never see it. Anything that must remain findable belongs in a Banner or in the page.
The default 5s timeout is a floor. Toasts with actions warrant longer, or persistent-until-dismissed.

doDont.dont: Toast what the user is already looking at — a row that visibly moved, an inline success state
doDont.why: A redundant announcement trains users to ignore toasts, and the one that mattered gets ignored with them.

doDont.do: Offer 'Undo' in a deletion toast and somewhere persistent
doDont.dont: Make the toast the only path to any action
doDont.why: The toast disappears in seconds by design. If missing it loses the user something, the action was never transient.

doDont.do: Reserve variant="danger" for failures that need action
doDont.dont: Announce successes assertively or promote every warning to danger
doDont.why: danger maps to role="alert", which interrupts the screen reader mid-sentence. Interruption is a budget; spend it on things that are actually wrong.

doDont.do: Keep it to a title and one short line
doDont.dont: Put paragraphs, forms, or a second action in a toast
doDont.why: Content that needs reading time or a decision outlives the timer. That is a Dialog (blocking) or a Banner (persistent), not a toast.

examples.title: Provider setup
examples.description: Mount once at the app root. The viewport, F6 shortcut, queue and timers all come with it.

examples.title: Fire and forget
examples.description: Works from anywhere — a fetch .catch, a store effect, a websocket handler. No hook, no context.
examples.code:
toast.success('Changes saved');
toast.error('Export failed', { description: 'The server did not respond.' });

examples.title: With an action
examples.description: One action, and it must also exist somewhere persistent — the toast is the shortcut, not the source.

examples.title: Dismiss programmatically
examples.description: toast() returns an id; dismiss it when the thing it announced becomes moot.
